intro: This branch studies circles in depth: the lines, angles and arcs (curved pieces) connected to them, and why they always relate in fixed ways. It ends by describing circles with equations on a grid.

V.8.01.what: Learning the names for lines and parts connected to a circle.

levels.a: Decides true or false about chords, radii and diameters.
levels.b: Tells minor arcs, major arcs and semicircles (half circles) apart.
levels.c: Describes two circles as sharing a center or as the same size.
levels.d: Picks out a radius, chord, diameter or tangent in a diagram.

V.8.02.what: Measuring arcs of a circle using central angles, the angles whose corner is at the center.

levels.a: Uses the fact that an arc and its center angle have the same measure.
levels.b: Adds or subtracts neighboring arcs and angles.
levels.c: Uses the fact that equal chords cut off equal arcs.
levels.d: Solves for x when the angles around the center add to 360 degrees.

V.8.03.what: Finding the length of an arc, the curved distance along part of a circle.

levels.a: Finds an arc's length as a fraction of the whole distance around.
levels.b: Finds an arc's exact length in terms of pi from the radius and angle.
levels.c: Works backwards from an arc length to the angle or radius.
levels.d: Solves everyday problems, like how far a clock hand's tip travels.

V.8.04.what: Finding the area of a sector, a pizza-slice shaped piece of a circle.

levels.a: Finds a sector's area as a fraction of the whole circle, or the reverse.
levels.b: Finds a sector's exact area in terms of pi.
levels.c: Finds the area between a chord and its arc by subtracting a triangle.
levels.d: Solves everyday problems, like the area a sprinkler waters.
levels.e: Works backwards from a sector's area to find the radius.
levels.f: Finds the exact area of the lens where two quarter circles in a square overlap.

V.8.05.what: Radians are a natural way to measure angles by comparing arc length to radius. A full turn is 2 times pi radians.

levels.a: Explains that one radian is the angle made by an arc as long as the radius.
levels.c: Finds arc length as radius times angle, with the angle in radians.
levels.d: Finds a sector's area using the angle in radians.

V.8.06.what: An angle with its corner on the circle is always half the arc it cuts off. This is the inscribed angle theorem.

levels.a: Finds an angle with its corner on the circle as half its arc, or the reverse.
levels.b: Identifies which of the three proof cases applies, based on where the center lies.
levels.c: Uses the fact that angles cutting off the same arc are equal.
levels.d: Solves for x using the half-the-arc rule.
levels.e: Adds radii to make an isosceles triangle and finds a hidden angle.
levels.f: Finds angles between corners of a regular polygon drawn inside a circle.

V.8.07.what: Useful results that follow from the inscribed angle theorem, such as an angle in a half circle always being a right angle.

levels.a: Uses the fact that an angle standing on a diameter is a right angle.
levels.b: Uses the fact that opposite angles of a four-sided shape inside a circle add to 180 degrees.
levels.c: Finds unknown angles in such shapes by solving for x.
levels.d: Finds the one wrong step in a proof about these facts.

V.8.08.what: A tangent line (one that just touches a circle) is always at right angles to the radius at that point.

levels.a: Uses the right angle between a tangent and the radius to find an angle.
levels.b: Uses the Pythagorean theorem to find exact lengths with a tangent.
levels.c: Tests whether a line touches the circle by checking for a right angle.
levels.d: Completes a short proof: names a missing reason or orders the steps.

V.8.09.what: The two tangent lines drawn to a circle from the same outside point are always equal in length.

levels.a: Uses equal tangent lengths from one point to find a length.
levels.b: Finds the perimeter of a triangle whose sides all touch a circle inside it.
levels.c: Solves for x using equal tangent lengths.
levels.d: Puts the steps of the proof that the two tangents are equal in order.
levels.e: Finds the radius of the circle that fits inside a right triangle.
levels.f: Finds the perimeter of a triangle cut off by a third tangent, or works backwards from it.

V.8.10.what: Facts about chords (lines joining two points on a circle) and how they relate to the center.

levels.a: Finds the one wrong step in a proof that a line from the center at right angles cuts a chord in half.
levels.b: Uses the fact that equal chords are equally far from the center.
levels.c: Finds a chord's length from the radius and its distance to the center.
levels.d: Orders the steps for finding a circle's center, and explains why they work.

V.8.11.what: When two chords cross inside a circle, the angle between them depends on the two arcs they cut off.

levels.a: Finds the angle where two chords cross inside a circle.
levels.b: Uses the rule that this angle is half the sum of the two arcs.
levels.c: Works backwards from the angle to find a missing arc.
levels.d: Completes the proof of the rule: names a missing reason or orders the steps.

V.8.12.what: When lines meet outside a circle, or a tangent meets a chord, the angle depends on the arcs in a similar way.

levels.a: Finds the angle where two lines cutting the circle meet outside it.
levels.b: Uses the half-the-difference rule with a tangent and a cutting line.
levels.c: Finds the angle between a tangent and a chord, which is half its arc.
levels.d: Solves for x using the half-the-difference rule.
levels.e: Uses the full 360 degrees of the circle to find the angle between two tangents.
levels.f: Finds angles when the circle is split into arcs in a given ratio.

V.8.13.what: When two chords cross, the two pieces of one chord multiply to the same answer as the two pieces of the other.

levels.a: Finds a missing piece where two chords cross, using equal products of the pieces.
levels.b: Picks the correct equation for the pieces.
levels.c: Solves for x, including pieces written as expressions.
levels.d: Completes the proof using similar triangles: names a missing reason or finds the wrong step.

V.8.14.what: Similar length rules for lines that cut through or touch a circle from an outside point.

levels.a: Finds a missing length for two cutting lines (secants) from an outside point.
levels.b: Finds a missing length for a tangent and a secant from the same point.
levels.c: Solves for x in these setups.
levels.d: Completes the proof of the rule: names a missing reason or finds the wrong step.
levels.e: Finds the radius when the cutting line passes through the center.
levels.f: Uses the 'power of a point' idea across two circles to find an exact tangent length.

V.8.15.what: Describing a circle with an equation on a grid, based on its center and radius.

levels.a: Reads the center and radius from a circle's equation.
levels.b: Builds the equation from the Pythagorean theorem, and tests whether a point is inside or outside.
levels.c: Writes the equation of a circle from the ends of a diameter.
levels.d: Finds tangent lines to a circle on a grid.

V.8.16.what: Recognizing a circle's equation when it has been multiplied out, and tidying it back to find the center and radius.

levels.a: Recognizes which multiplied-out equation is a circle.
levels.b: Completes the square for both x and y to tidy the equation.
levels.c: Reads the center and radius from the tidied equation.
levels.d: Finds the circle that passes through three given points.

V.8.17.what: All circles are the same shape, just scaled. That is why pi, the ratio of distance around to distance across, is the same for every circle.

levels.a: Finds the scale factor that shrinks or stretches one circle onto another.
levels.b: Explains why distance around divided by distance across is the same for every circle.
levels.c: Traps pi between the perimeters of shapes drawn inside and around a circle, as Archimedes did.
levels.d: Slices a circle into thin wedges and rearranges them into a near-rectangle to find its area.
